Issued at 318 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

Dominant single lake effect band continues to affect extreme NW 
Indiana early this morning in the Gary vicinity. Some synoptic 
enhanced light precipitation extends east across the local area from 
South bend vicinity into southern Lower Michigan. This area of light 
precip appears tied to a lagging secondary low level baroclinic zone 
and weak accompanying low level frontogenesis forcing. Through the 
morning, this band of precip should tend to diminish with near term 
low level fgen progs depicting some weakening of this synoptic 
forcing. 

The dominant band across far NW Indiana may try to exhibit some 
slight eastward adjustment after daybreak as a broader synoptic 
scale upper level short wave drops south across the Mid MS Valley. 
Some subtle uptick in low level fgen forcing could aid in some 
eastward development this morning as 950-900 mb speed convergence 
associated with better northerly flow working south across western 
Great Lakes interacts with thermally modified mass fields over 
far southern Lake Michigan. The more pronounced low level cold 
advection this morning working across the western shore of Lake 
Michigan will continue to allow for development of a weak 
northerly low level jet across western Lake Michigan and a 
pronounced horizontal shearing zone across the western third of 
the lake. This should keep the higher precip rates and dominant 
single band anchored along this horizontal shearing instability 
axis through the morning hours to the west of the local area. 
With some uncertainty in other synoptic factors coming into play
discussed above, did maintain some low to mid range chance PoPs
extreme west, but not expecting any snow accumulation locally 
at this time.

By this afternoon southward passage of another upper level trough 
across the western Great Lakes will likely allow for better lake 
effect precip to shift back to the Chicago metro area into portions 
of far NW Indiana. Did maintain high chance/low likely rain PoPs 
across far western portions of the forecast area this afternoon, but 
it is possible this can be adjusted downward depending on trends. 
Otherwise for today, little temperature recovery is expected given 
weak ongoing cold advection and cloud cover. Between clouds across 
the west and a possible maintenance of higher cloud cover in east 
with Lake Huron connection, a zone from southwest Lower Michigan 
into the US-15 corridor could experience some sun today. Highs will 
likely be limited to the low-mid 40s.

For tonight, there should be a lull in the parade of stronger short 
waves rotating through the broad negative upper height anomaly which 
should allow for some backing of the flow to eventually take better 
lake effect precip chances into NW Indiana/SW Lower MI later tonight 
into Saturday AM. Thermal profiles and sfc/near sfc wet bulbs do 
appear on the marginal side of rain vs snow in modified airmass 
downwind of warmer Lake Michigan waters. It also appears by late 
tonight, some drying of the DGZ should take place which will make 
snowfall production less efficient and possibly promote more of a 
cellular character. Did maintain some light accums across La Porte 
of less than a half inch across mainly grassy areas farther inland, 
but currently not expecting any significant travel impacts. Lake 
effect rain showers in scattered fashion may continue into midday 
Saturday but should become less organized and cellular through time.

A weak short wave spilling down the central CONUS/south central 
Canadian ridge may cause some isolated-scattered light lake effect 
rain again by Saturday evening, but otherwise dry conditions are 
expected through the remainder of the weekend as a stable longwave 
pattern featuring central CONUS ridging remains established. This 
pattern will be characterized by weak baroclinicity and little day 
to day thermal advection. This will promote continued below normal 
temperatures through the weekend. Looking ahead to next week, the 
broad eastern CONUS negative upper height anomaly should finally 
begin to break down allowing for eastward progression of the 
longwave ridge as stronger Pacific systems moves inland. 
Temperatures should moderate back to above normal in this pattern 
for middle and latter portions of next work week. While thee are 
some indications a stronger eastern Pacific wave will dampen the 
longwave ridge, better quality low level moisture should remain 
confined to the southern/central Plains so a dry forecast has been 
maintained through this forecast valid period.
